title: Bota Singh Writes a Defiant Toll Letter

blocks.text: Bota Singh wrote a letter that turns hiding into open defiance. He announces that he and his companion are openly stopping traffic, demanding an anna for a bullock cart and a penny for an ass in order to show that the Khalsa still refuses erasure.

The letter is meant as a public insult to Mughal authority, so the Nawab dispatches troops at once. Yet the page frames the challenge less as robbery than as deliberate political theater staged by men who want the state to face them directly.

When the soldiers arrive, the Singhs refuse compromise. They insist that the confrontation should happen face to face, making their small roadside stand into a declaration that Sikh courage can still command the road.
